## The single weakest link (judgement of this task)

**U3/U5b: the deployed sink.ts, the only component that writes committed state.** It is not only unproved; it is known to be wrong (machine-checked counterexample U5r-CONTRAST; Node runs; every differential control pair with the real sink diverges). The night produced a much stronger REPAIR, but only as a draft: in the V6 design the model-level step needs no signing or collision hypothesis for "committed => approved" (T-V6-STEP, T-V6-BYTES-L0, both reviewed), and its TypeScript shell agrees with the compiled core on 3,500 sequences. Adoption is blocked by an open owner question about the meaning of "approved" at the sink (CTX-SINK, B-10), by one suite row that needs a new expectation, by the unproved TypeScript shell (TS-LOOP-IS-FOLD), and by ADMISSION (main is not protected). Until an owner applies it, every MC edge about the sink is about a model or a draft, and the deployed segment rests on TESTED evidence with a known defect. Runner-up: ADMISSION (S1, E1-E6).
